result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B separates required from optional steps more clearly ('Start here' vs 'Do these when you're ready'), adds a 'Finish for now' exit, and explains why. A's three stages still read as one nine-step sequence. Neither answer ties the first steps to placing a first order, and neither says deferred steps will come back when the admin first needs them. B also loses a point for inventing 'about 10 minutes'. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): A splits the steps into a short 'Start here' set and a 'Do these when you're ready' set, and replaces 'Click Finish when done' with 'Finish for now', so it is clearer that the later steps are optional. B's stages ('Then set up ordering', 'Then set up your team and tools') still read like one nine-step sequence, though it does name Settings as the place to come back to. Both keep all nine steps on screen and don't tie the first steps to placing a first order; both miscount the original feature list as 14 (it is 12), and A adds an unsupported 'about 10 minutes' estimate.
